propositions: Operators resort to --force to close 25+ administrative tickets (duplicate, obsolete, wontfix, stale-premise) because the completion-verification path only covers bugs and the failure message does not disclose the attested-disposition alternative.

The existing close-class mechanism restricts non-bug closes to {duplicate, not_a_bug, escalated} and gates obsolete/superseded/wontfix to bugs only, leaving non-bug tickets without a truthful administrative exit.
The close-gate refusal message must enumerate the valid --class values for each ticket type and explicitly surface the administrative-disposition path to prevent blind --force usage.

Administrative closes with reason-required classes (obsolete, wontfix) must enforce reason capture at the write layer (transition_core), persist it as a distinct close_reason key (not force_close_reason), and skip completion verification.
The disposition attestation must sign reason-only administrative closes with a manifest line carrying class and reason text, maintaining unsigned-close detection as a RED signal.

Non-administrative close classes (not_a_bug, escalated, regression) remain bug-only vocabulary; non-bug tickets refusing these values must name the allowed administrative alternatives in the error message.
